name: millwright
description: Millwright — an MCP server for Linux and ROS 2 development: shell, file editing, background jobs, ROS 2 introspection, simulation, and workspace builds, with a simulation-first safety posture.
long_description:
Millwright is an execution layer that lets the model work as a Linux developer and a ROS 2 robotics developer through one consistent tool schema: run bounded shell commands, edit files by exact search/replace, manage background jobs, introspect the ROS 2 graph, sample topics, launch and restart nodes it owns, scaffold packages, and run colcon builds with real compiler errors returned on failure.

ROS tools require a ROS 2 installation (validated against ROS 2 Lyrical on Ubuntu 26.04; Jazzy/Humble should work via the setup-script setting). Set `ros_setup_script` so the server can source your ROS environment - on Windows this path is inside your WSL distro and commands are routed through WSL automatically. All ROS tools degrade gracefully (clear `available: false` message) when ROS is absent; the Linux tools work everywhere a POSIX shell exists.

tools.name: workbench_shell
tools.description: Run a shell command for the user's own project environment (prefer this over any built-in/simulated sandbox when the user means their machine). By DEFAULT (sandbox_mode 'docker') it runs INSIDE a Docker container with the user's workspace folder mounted — writes to the workspace are real, but the rest of the host isn't visible and tools/state are the container's; with sandbox_mode 'off' it runs directly on the host. The result's `sandboxed` field reports which. Bounded output (~200 lines), hard timeout, destructive-command blocklist. Blocking; long-running work belongs in job_start.

tools.name: workspace_edit
tools.description: Edit a file by exact search/replace. Refuses zero-match and ambiguous multi-match edits (unless replace_all) and leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged on any refusal; replacement text is inserted literally.

tools.name: job_start
tools.description: Start a long-running command (server, watcher, sim) as a tracked background job; returns a job_id immediately.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List all background jobs started by this server (Linux or ROS) with status and start time.

tools.name: job_logs
tools.description: Tail recent stdout/stderr of a background job to confirm it came up cleanly or diagnose a failure.

tools.name: job_stop
tools.description: Stop a background job gracefully: SIGINT, then SIGKILL after the grace period.

tools.name: ros_nodes
tools.description: List active ROS 2 nodes (de-duplicated), optionally filtered by a name substring.

tools.name: ros_graph
tools.description: Return the ROS 2 computational graph (nodes + topics) as structured JSON; optionally include hidden topics.

tools.name: ros_topic
tools.description: Capture up to max_messages from a topic over ONE persistent subscription, stopping at N messages or when the overall timeout_sec budget elapses (short reads flagged timed_out). Messages are clean YAML documents (no --- separator); the subscription process is confirmed dead before the call returns. message_type is accepted but ignored - the type is resolved from the live topic.

tools.name: ros_launch
tools.description: Launch a ROS 2 package/launch file as a tracked background job. Required before ros_restart will work for that node.

tools.name: ros_restart
tools.description: Stop and relaunch a ROS 2 node previously started via ros_launch. Refuses to touch processes this server did not launch (deliberate safety boundary).

tools.name: ros_pkg_new
tools.description: Scaffold a new ROS 2 package via `ros2 pkg create` inside a workspace src/ directory (created if missing); choose ament_cmake or ament_python, declare dependencies, optionally scaffold a starter node.

tools.name: ros_build
tools.description: Build a ROS 2 workspace with `colcon build` (optionally --packages-select). Bounded and truncated like workbench_shell; on failure returns success:false with the real compiler errors in stderr.

ros_setup_script.title: ROS 2 setup script path
ros_setup_script.description: Example: /opt/ros/lyrical/setup.bash (use your distro's name). Windows: this is a Linux path inside your WSL distro. No ROS? Leave blank. Details in README.

wsl_distro.title: WSL distro for ROS (Windows only)
wsl_distro.description: Windows only: the WSL distribution where ROS 2 is installed. ROS commands are routed into it via wsl.exe when a setup script is configured. Ignored on macOS/Linux.

shell_bin.title: Shell for workbench_shell
shell_bin.description: Shell binary used by workbench_shell (invoked as `<shell> -lc "..."`). Default: bash. On Windows without bash on PATH, set the full path to Git Bash, e.g. C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe.

sandbox_mode.title: Sandbox mode (docker or off)
sandbox_mode.description: 'docker' (default): shell commands and builds run in Docker containers; file edits are limited to the workspace folder. 'off': everything runs directly on your machine, no isolation. Details in README.

workspace_dir.title: Workspace folder
workspace_dir.description: The project folder Millwright works in. Mounted into sandbox containers, and the only place file edits are allowed while sandboxing is on. Windows: pick a folder inside your WSL distro (\\wsl.localhost\...).

workbench_network.title: Sandbox network (all or none)
workbench_network.description: 'all' (default): sandboxed commands have internet access (npm/pip/apt work). 'none': no network inside the sandbox. Builds always run with no network either way.

sandbox_cpus.title: Sandbox CPU limit
sandbox_cpus.description: Max CPU cores a sandbox container may use (docker --cpus; a decimal like '1.5' is allowed). Default '2' keeps a runaway process from pegging your machine while leaving builds usable. Raise it for faster builds on many-core hosts.
